topics.topic: Startup A08 rule 5 validation without an operation or proposed ports
questions: With no operation name or proposed ports supplied at startup, exactly which A08 rule 5 checks are applied, and are they applied to every capability or only to the service-record structure?
Which A08 rule 5 checks apply at startup when this operation has a service and selected instance but no operation name or proposed ports?

Because A08 rule 5 contains checks for a particular operation and proposed ports, which checks can `check_installed_instances` perform without an operation or proposal, which capability entries are examined, and in what order?

judgement.why: The topic asks the same startup-validation question, and neither the relevant passages nor the reopening change altered it.

precedent.topic: Manifest validation rules applied to installed instances at startup
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: The later notes limit startup validation to credential-bearing services, ordered by service_id, and to top-level service-record checks plus the selected instance's credential-header collision.

topics.topic: Allowed service base URLs and joining them with operation paths
questions: Are user information, query, fragment and non-root base paths allowed in `api_base_url`, and exactly how are trailing slashes and the operation path combined?
May `api_base_url` contain user-info, a path, query, fragment, percent escapes, an IPv6 zone, or multiple trailing slashes, and exactly how is it joined to the operation path?

judgement.why: The topic repeats the same base-URL grammar and path-joining question on unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Allowed API base URL components and operation-path joining semantics
quotes:
the installation selects no instance for the service or that
   instance has no `api_base_url` — one that is not an absolute `http` or
   `https` URL with a host counts as none — or names one required header
   twice, or names one the kernel sets itself (`host`, `accept-encoding`,
   `content-type`, `content-length`, A10 rule 7) other than `host`, which an
   instance may set instead of the kernel (A10 rule 7), names compared without
   regard to case — at send time both are A09 rule 6's `required_header_repeated`
   —, or has a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character — at send time `required_header_invalid`;

The
   URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared
   path, which must start with one `/` and contain no `//`, no `.` or `..`
   segment, no `?` or `#`, and no scheme or host; a `{` or `}` appears only in a
   placeholder, which is one whole segment `{name}` whose name is not empty and
   contains no `{`, `}` or `/`, and no name is a placeholder twice; a path that
   does not is not invocable (A08 rule 3). Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they
   stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.

Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
   The host judged here, the one connected to, and for `https` the server name
   sent and verified, are always those of `api_base_url`; a required `Host`
   header (A10 rule 7) changes only the header sent.

`host` — the authority of `api_base_url` exactly as the manifest writes it,
   not normalized (A09 rule 1), unless the instance's required headers name
   `host`, in which case that required header is sent instead, its value
   verbatim, and is the only `host` —, `accept-encoding: identity` (A09 rule 3),
precedent.why: The texts constrain an absolute HTTP(S) URL and simple concatenation but do not close the accepted URL grammar, slash handling, component interaction, or loopback classification.

topics.topic: Encoding or rejection of unsafe multipart port names and filenames
questions: How are quotes, backslashes, control characters and non-ASCII characters in a port name represented or refused in multipart `name` and `filename` parameters?
How are quotes, backslashes, controls, non-ASCII characters and other unsafe characters in a port name represented in multipart header parameters?

judgement.why: Multipart header-parameter escaping and rejection are wire-encoding and format contract questions for State 6.

topics.topic: Privacy requirements for the store data directory and its contents
questions: What exact ownership and permission conditions define a private data directory and private existing contents for the open_store start check?
What exact ownership, permission and traversal checks make the data directory and everything in it private, including subdirectories, regular files, ACLs and unexpected file types?

quotes: open_store: [BEHAVIOR] MUST run, in this order, stopping at the first failure: take an exclusive non-blocking lock on a lock file inside data_directory, opened without following links and held for the life of the process; check that data_directory and everything inside it are owned by the process's effective user and grant no permission to group or others; walk the directory without following links and find no symbolic link; then remove the module's own temporary files left by an interrupted publish and every file of the content-addressed area whose digest no StoredValue and no file fixture record names, and create the database schema, the content-addressed area and the spool area when absent.

open_store: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise RefusedError whose reason names the failed check: data_directory does not exist (it is never created here), lock held by another process, directory not private (naming the first offending path), or symbolic link found (naming its path); it removes and creates nothing when a check fails.
judgement.why: The later notes define privacy by effective-user ownership and no permissions for group or others across the directory and all contents, with a separate no-symlink traversal check.

topics.topic: Resolution and reading of a configured manifest revision
questions: How must bindings read `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` at `manifest_revision`, rather than silently reading some other filesystem state?
What does reading a file “at” the configured revision mean operationally, and how is the revision resolved without silently reading the working tree or another revision?

quotes:
8. **The manifest at a revision**: `manifest_location` is a directory inside a
git repository and `manifest_revision` a commit of it; `bindings` reads
`<service_id>.json` of that directory at that commit as a git object, never
from the working tree, so a record changes only with the configured revision
(A08 rules 1 and 6).
judgement.why: The later contract requires reading the manifest record as a Git object at the configured commit, never from the working tree.

topics.topic: Unit and stage used to calculate masked failure-detail length
questions: Is the disclosed length the number of UTF-8 bytes, Unicode scalar values, or characters after replacement and truncation?
Is the disclosed length the UTF-8 byte length, Unicode code-point count, grapheme count, or the original pre-truncation length?

quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
judgement.why: The later notes specify the masked length as the UTF-8 byte length of the stored failure_detail.

topics.topic: Canonical JSON representation hashed for effect idempotency keys
questions: What exact JSON value is hashed: an object keyed by field name, a list of values in manifest order, or a list of name/value pairs?

topics.topic: Canonical public identity of a SpooledFile
questions: Is a SpooledFile's public identity all M22 meaning facts or only the producing-position key listed by `read_spooled_file`?

topics.topic: Canonical request representation hashed for approval requests
questions: What exact JSON structure and field names represent the method, URL, headers and the JSON-or-multipart body description before hashing?

topics.topic: Controls preventing nondeterministic sandbox observations
questions: What prevents code from deriving output from untrapped process and interpreter observations such as object identities, process metadata, filesystem metadata, locale or runtime paths?

topics.topic: Definition of whitespace and control characters in header and credential validation
questions: Which exact Unicode or byte characters count as whitespace and control characters for required-header and credential validation?

topics.topic: Exact credential trailing-newline removal rule
questions: Does one trailing newline mean LF only, one CRLF sequence, either LF or CRLF, and are additional trailing newline sequences retained or removed?

topics.topic: Exact sandbox failure details for each failure class
questions: What exact detail is returned for an exception, abnormal exit, contract violation, trap, timeout and resource exhaustion, including the separator and whether an empty detail is present or absent?

topics.topic: How loopback hosts are identified for the plain-HTTP exception
questions: Is loopback determined only from a literal IP address in the URL, from special hostnames such as `localhost`, or after DNS resolution?

topics.topic: Outcome precedence when a final HTTP response body is incomplete
questions: If a valid final status and headers arrive but the body times out, resets or ends before its declared length, does the transport-failure row win, or does the known status row decide the effect outcome?

topics.topic: Pagination when a repair-view implementation set exceeds continuation-token capacity
questions: How can pagination continue for a slot whose implementation set cannot fit in a bounded continuation-token string?

topics.topic: Referential validation of embedded relation elements
questions: For relations such as executions, approvals or attempts of an element, and active grant of a flow-version node, does store validate that the embedded node or mapped element exists, or trust the caller and return an empty relation when no matching records exist?

topics.topic: Repair-view behavior when a slot has no implementations
questions: What does get_repair_view do when the slot has no implementations and therefore its executed_implementation filter set is empty?

topics.topic: Required input and expected-output port sets for authored trial cases
questions: Must authored inputs contain exactly every contract input and no extra names, and when `expected_outputs` is present must it contain exactly every output, or may it specify only a subset?

topics.topic: Rollback to the current implementation when its verdict is no longer admitted
questions: If corpus growth left the currently active implementation without an admitted verdict over the current corpus, does roll_back_slot naming that same current implementation return its activation unchanged or refuse it for lacking the verdict?

topics.topic: Sandboxed agent access to runtime and exchange filesystems
questions: May agent code directly open or enumerate files in the runtime and exchange directory, or are those locations accessible only to the runner and import machinery?

topics.topic: Service manifest JSON schema
questions: What exact JSON structure, field types and optionality does a service manifest use for capabilities, instances, exposed HTTP routes, required headers, instance classes and idempotency keys?

topics.topic: Storage or return location of the NodeExecution diagnostic code
questions: Where is the machine-significant detail code stored or returned separately from the bounded service or exception text in `failure_detail`?

topics.topic: Timestamp semantics for NodeExecutions where no execution or send begins
questions: What timestamps are recorded for `operation_failed` pre-send checks, `refused_by_owner`, `skipped_by_guard`, `upstream_failed`, receiving-node contract violations and an empty mapped node, where no execution or send begins?

topics.topic: Validation and rejection of configured service identifiers
questions: Must service identifiers appearing in installation selections and credentials satisfy SERVICE_ID_PATTERN, and which operation refuses an invalid configured identifier before any manifest path is built?

topics.topic: Validation and transmission of declared HTTP path literals
questions: What characters and percent escapes are valid in the literal portions of a declared path, and are those literals sent verbatim, percent-encoded, or refused when they are not already a valid URI path?

topics.topic: Whether approval continuation guarantees an HTTP send
questions: Does approving guarantee that an HTTP request leaves the kernel during the same call, or does the call merely reach the element again and possibly end in operation_failed or another owner_approval wait without sending?

topics.topic: Whether direct record reads return complete records or only listed fields
questions: Do these reads return the complete State 1 record, including identity, owner links, creator or author and timestamps, or only the fields individually listed in each Outputs section?

topics.topic: Whether the sandbox output-byte limit is aggregate, per-output, or both
questions: Is `output_bytes` one aggregate limit across all outputs of a call, a separate limit applied to every output, or both?

topics.topic: Wire encoding and representability of non-ASCII HTTP header values
questions: What bytes are sent for non-ASCII required-header or credential values, and are values that cannot be represented by the chosen HTTP library refused?
